properties.name: A computed fact supports a claim only through its kept computation record, never through a check someone set passing by hand
properties.statement:
A check made by computation names its kept calc record: an Artifact with its checksum. Then:
- it reads passing as a premise only while that record exists, its checksum matches, and the record states the result;
- with no record, it reads "asserted", not passing.

A host such as flo2 can re-run the record on request.

From the primes trial (fact:the-primes-trial-rung-1-ran-on-flo2-io-and-its-friction-names-what-counts-2026-10-17, item 1). @ajs, 2026-10-17: "I want to fix all 7…", choosing "Bound to its record".
